## Claims
- [proved] For \(r,q\ge1\), with \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) the \(q^r\)-box quotient,
  \[
  A\cong\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}),
  \]
  where \(E(-t)H(t)=1\). Indeed,
  \[
  I_{r,q}=(h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots,e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}).
  \]
- [proved] For the \(i=j=1\) case, \(J_v=A_+\), and, with \(m=\min(r,q)\),
  \[
  A_+/A_+^2\cong\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_k\cong\mathbb Z^m.
  \]
- [proved] In \(A_+/A_+^2\),
  \[
  \overline e_k=(-1)^{k-1}\overline h_k\qquad(1\le k\le m).
  \]
  Hence both \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_m\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) map to integral bases.
- [proved] The two specialized families are
  \[
  \{h_1,\ldots,h_m\},\qquad \{e_1,\ldots,e_m\};
  \]
  each minimally generates \(J_v=A_+\). Thus the \(i=j=1\) family, equivalently \(v_{r,r,r,r+q}\) for \(r,q\ge1\), is settled.
- [source-backed] The supplied project documentation records the corresponding free-indecomposables assertion as only suspected in the general rectangular case. [source-6, lines 56-70]

## Strategy
Write \(I=I_{r,q}\). Since \(h_k=s_{(k)}\) for \(k>q\), and \(e_k=s_{(1^k)}\) for \(k>r\), the ideal
\[
K=(h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots,e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q})
\]
lies in \(I\).

Conversely, let \(\lambda\not\subseteq q^r\). If \(\lambda_1>q\), the Jacobi--Trudi determinant for \(s_\lambda\) has first row consisting of \(h_a\) with \(a>q\), so \(s_\lambda\in K\). If \(\lambda_1\le q\) but \(\ell(\lambda)>r\), then modulo \((h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots)\), the coefficient identity from \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) inductively gives
\[
e_N\in(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q})\qquad(N>r).
\]
The dual Jacobi--Trudi determinant has first row consisting of such \(e_N\), so again \(s_\lambda\in K\). Thus \(I=K\), yielding the stated presentation.

Let \(P=\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]\), \(P_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\), and \(R=(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q})\). Then
\[
A_+/A_+^2\cong P_+/(P_+^2+R).
\]
Modulo \(P_+^2\), the identity \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) gives
\[
e_k\equiv(-1)^{k-1}h_k\quad(k\le q).
\]
Therefore the linear parts of the defining relations are precisely
\[
(-1)^{r+\ell-1}h_{r+\ell}\qquad
(1\le\ell\le q,\ r+\ell\le q).
\]
They eliminate exactly \(h_{r+1},\ldots,h_q\) when \(r<q\), and impose no relation on \(h_1,\ldots,h_m\). Hence the quotient is freely generated by their classes.

For \(i=j=1\), one has \(a=m-1\) and \(b=1\). The two partition intervals become respectively
\[
(1)\subseteq(k)\subseteq(m),\qquad
(1)\subseteq(1^k)\subseteq(1^m),
\]
giving the two stated families. Their images are bases of \(A_+/A_+^2\). Graded Nakayama gives generation of \(A_+\), and deletion of any member fails after quotienting by \(A_+^2\); hence both families are minimal.

## Gaps
- This proof assumes the box-quotient model and the \(i=j=1\) identification \(J_v=A_+\) stated in the task.
